name: tsw-safety-united-kingdom-thejag
title: Safety systems · United Kingdom
eyebrow: Signals and train protection · Train Sim World · TCA Quadrant Airbus
sources: RSSB GERT8000 Rule Book (modules S1, S3, TW1)
en.wikipedia: UK railway signalling, AWS, TPWS, Driver's Safety Device, DRA

paragraphs: British colour-light signals show **how many sections ahead are clear**, not the speed: green, double yellow, single yellow, red. Speed comes from the **lineside speed signs** and the route knowledge. Junction indicators and route indicators show a diverging route. **AWS** warns you at every caution, **TPWS** stops you at a red signal or an overspeed, the **DSD / vigilance** checks that you are awake. Quadrant controls are from TheJAG's UK profiles.

items.name: AWS
items.summary: A magnet 180 m before colour-light and distant signals and warning boards. **Bell / chime** = clear (green). **Horn** = caution, red or a speed warning: acknowledge within about **2.7 s** or the brakes apply. The black and yellow **sunflower** then shows you did.
items.quadrant: **Gear lever** = AWS reset; left aux square = AWS (/ TPWS) isolation

items.name: TPWS
items.summary: Loops at red signals, speed restrictions and buffer stops. **Train stop**: passing a red signal brakes the train. **Overspeed sensor**: approaching too fast brakes it. Brake demand lamp flashes; the brakes release 60 s after the demand.
items.quadrant: Shares the AWS isolation (left aux square) on most units; Train Stop Override in the cab

items.name: DSD / vigilance
items.full: Driver's Safety Device, Driver Vigilance Device (DVD)
items.summary: A pedal or handle held while driving; let go and the train brakes. Vigilance adds an alarm about every 60 s that you acknowledge.
items.quadrant: Gear lever acknowledges in TSW (Q); right aux square = DSD / DVD isolation on most units

items.name: DRA
items.summary: A button you set when stopped at a red signal or a platform with the signal at danger: it cuts traction until you release it.
items.where: Units and locos that have one
items.quadrant: Round aux on the 385 and the 90; in the cab on the others

items.name: Tripcock
items.summary: A trainstop arm next to each LU signal is raised at red; passing it trips the tripcock on the train and brakes it.
items.quadrant: 1972: **ENG 1** tripcock reset, gear lever valve reset

items.name: TVM 430 / ETCS
items.summary: HS1 uses French TVM 430 cab signals (no lineside signals) KVB in the St Pancras area (not simulated). No TSW 7 UK route in this collection has ETCS.

sections.title: Colour-light signals (4-aspect)
sections.note: Rays = flashing. A 3-aspect signal has no top yellow and no double yellow.

items.name: Green
items.meaning: Proceed; the next signal shows a proceed aspect.
items.drive: Line speed. AWS bell.

items.name: Double yellow
items.meaning: Preliminary caution: the next signal shows single yellow.
items.drive: AWS horn: acknowledge. Start to brake.

items.name: Single yellow
items.meaning: Caution: be prepared to stop at the next signal.
items.drive: Acknowledge AWS; brake to stop at the next signal.

items.name: Red
items.meaning: Danger: stop.
items.drive: Stop before the signal; TPWS train stop.

items.name: Flashing double yellow
items.meaning: Diverging junction ahead at a speed; next signal flashing single yellow.
items.drive: Acknowledge; brake toward the junction speed.

items.name: Flashing single yellow
items.meaning: Next signal shows a junction indicator for a diverging route.
items.drive: Be at the turnout speed at the junction.

items.name: Junction indicator
items.meaning: Five white lights: the route diverges to the left (or right).
items.drive: Take the turnout at its speed sign.

items.name: Route indicator
items.meaning: Theatre box: a lit letter or number names the route or platform.
items.drive: Check the route is the one you expect.

items.name: Position light subsidiary
items.meaning: Red with two white lights: pass the red signal; the line ahead may be occupied.
items.drive: Pass at caution, ready to stop short of any obstruction.

items.name: Ground signal: stop
items.meaning: Two reds horizontal (older signals: red and white): stop.
items.drive: Stop short of it.

items.name: Ground signal: proceed
items.meaning: Two white lights at 45°: proceed (shunt).
items.drive: Proceed at caution to the next signal or limit.

sections.title: Semaphores
sections.note: Stop arm: red with a white stripe. Distant arm: yellow with a black chevron and fishtail end. Lower quadrant arms drop for off, upper quadrant arms rise.

items.name: Stop: on
items.meaning: Arm horizontal: danger.
items.drive: Stop before the signal.

items.name: Stop: off (lower quadrant)
items.meaning: Arm lowered: proceed.
items.drive: Proceed.

items.name: Stop: off (upper quadrant)
items.meaning: Arm raised: proceed.
items.drive: Proceed.

items.name: Distant: on
items.meaning: Caution: the stop signal ahead may be at danger.
items.drive: AWS horn: acknowledge, be ready to stop.

items.name: Distant: off
items.meaning: All the stop signals of the box ahead are off.
items.drive: AWS bell; proceed.

items.name: Speed sign
items.meaning: Permissible speed from here, in mph (older lines: yellow cut-out figures).
items.drive: Lower: by the sign. Higher: once the rear has passed.

items.name: PSR warning
items.meaning: A lower permissible speed ahead; AWS magnet 180 m before it.
items.drive: AWS horn: acknowledge, brake to the speed.

items.name: TSR warning
items.meaning: Temporary restriction ahead; AWS magnet. Two white discs (flashing white lights on lit boards).
items.drive: AWS horn: acknowledge, brake to the speed.

items.name: TSR speed
items.meaning: Temporary limit starts here.
items.drive: Be at the speed by the board.

items.name: TSR end
items.meaning: Temporary limit ends.
items.drive: Accelerate once the rear has passed.

items.name: AWS cancelling
items.meaning: An AWS magnet for the other direction: no warning for you. Yellow with a black cross at a TSR.
items.drive: Ignore any AWS indication here.

sections.title: AWS and TPWS at a glance
head: Event
In the cab
What to do
rows: **AWS reset** (gear lever) within about 2.7 s; sunflower turns yellow and black
Stop, acknowledge, then release the brake
Brake demand lamp flashes, brakes apply
Acknowledge (lamp goes steady); report to the signaller; the brakes release 60 s after the demand
Stop, hold the DSD / acknowledge, release the brake

sections.title: How to drive under AWS, TPWS and the DSD

blocks.title: Approaching a caution
steps: Double yellow: AWS horn, press **AWS reset** (gear lever). Start braking.
Single yellow: AWS horn again, reset. Brake to stop at the next signal.
Keep below the TPWS trigger speed on the approach to the red; stop short.

blocks.title: At a red signal
steps: Stop before the signal. Set the **DRA** if you are waiting.
Contact the signaller if the signal does not clear.
To pass at danger with authority, press **Train Stop Override** (in the cab): it covers the train stop for about 20 s (60 s on the 66), never the overspeed sensor.
Release the DRA when the signal clears, then take power.

blocks.title: TPWS intervention
steps: Brakes apply and the brake demand lamp flashes.
Leave the controls; let the train stop.
Acknowledge with **AWS reset**: the lamp goes steady. Report to the signaller; the brakes release 60 s after the demand.

blocks.title: Speed restrictions
bullets: PSR and TSR warning boards carry an AWS magnet: horn, reset, brake.
Be at the speed by the speed sign; TPWS overspeed sensors guard some restrictions.
Higher speed only once the rear of the train has passed the sign.

blocks.title: DSD and vigilance
steps: Keep the DSD / DVD switched in (right aux square: isolation off).
When the vigilance buzzer sounds, acknowledge with the **gear lever**.
Missed: the brakes apply; stop, acknowledge, release and drive on.

blocks.title: London Underground (1938, 1972 Stock)
bullets: Signals: red / green; a trainstop arm is raised at red.
Passing a red trips the tripcock: emergency brake.
A trip counts as a signal passed at danger: stop, report, then reset the tripcock (**ENG 1**) and the valve (**gear lever**, 1972) and continue slowly.

sections.title: Before departure:
sections.text: AWS / TPWS and DSD isolation lights out: on most units the aux squares are isolation switches, unlit = in service (the 380 starts isolated). Flying Scotsman: left aux lit = AWS on; the LMS steam locos have no AWS. DRA released, the signal off.
